newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Argentina calls for Third World trade preferences.
newsitem.headline: Argentina calls for Third World trade preferences.

text.p: Argentine Vice-President Carlos Ruckauf urged Third World countries to pool their resources, and to trade on preferential lines in order to survive in an increasingly competitive world economic environment.

"One of our main challenges today is to find a pragmatic and focused consensus allowing us to tackle the problem of development in the context of an increasing globalized world economy," he said when he addressed a trade promotion conference of developing nations called Group of 15 (G-15).

"We are convinced of the need to revitalise the Global System of Preferences among developing countries as it is the most suitable and appropriate mechanism at our disposal for the generation of trade among the developing countries," he said.
The World Trade Organisation discourages preferential trade arrangements and wants them to be extended to all if chosen.
Ruckauf called for the creation of new trade bridges between regional and subregional schemes in order to open up new opportunities for increased economic relations.

Argentina, he said, was actively contributing towards the goal of increased trade among developing countries, pointing that 60 percent of its exports last year were to countries in Latin America and a further 30 percent to other developing countries, particularly Asia.
"Therefore...our interest in increasing trade among the developing countries is neither merely theoretical nor ideological, for it is our own growth which depends on it," he said.

Despite holding onto its original name, the G-15 now groups 16 member states, namely Algeria, Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Egypt, India, Indonesia, Jamaica, Malaysia, Mexico, Nigeria, Senegal, Peru, Venezuela, Yugoslavia and Zimbabwe.
